legend.intro: The symbols next to each dish mean:
legend.vegetarian: Vegetarian dish, no meat or fish.
legend.vegan: Vegan dish, no ingredients of animal origin.

fior-di-latte.desc: Fresh cow's-milk mozzarella, milder than the buffalo kind. Contains milk.

mozzarella-bufala.desc: Mozzarella made from water-buffalo milk: creamier and tangier. Contains milk.

provola.desc: A stretched-curd cow's-milk cheese, here in its smoked version. Contains milk.

stracciatella.desc: The creamy heart of burrata: shreds of stretched curd in cream. Contains milk.

burrata.desc: A cheese from Puglia: a stretched-curd pouch with a creamy centre. Contains milk.

ricotta.desc: A fresh, mildly sweet dairy product made from whey. Contains milk.

grana-padano.desc: A long-aged hard cheese, grainy and savoury. Contains milk.

pecorino.desc: A sheep's-milk cheese, salty and well aged. Contains milk.

gorgonzola.desc: An Italian blue cheese from cow's milk: creamy, blue-veined, boldly flavoured. Contains milk.

caciocavallo.desc: An aged stretched-curd cheese with an intense flavour. Contains milk.

casciotta.desc: A semi-aged cheese from the Marche region, made with sheep's and cow's milk. Contains milk.

speck.desc: Smoked, cured ham from Alto Adige. Pork.

guanciale.desc: Cured pork cheek, fattier and more intense than pancetta. Pork.

capocollo.desc: A cured cold cut made from the neck of the pig. Pork.

mortadella.desc: A cooked cold cut from Bologna: pink, mild, often studded with pistachios. Pork.

ventricina.desc: A spicy cured sausage from Abruzzo and Molise, made with chilli. Pork.

fassona.desc: A prized Piedmontese cattle breed, known for its lean meat. Beef.

dop.desc: Protected Designation of Origin: an EU mark for products made entirely in one defined area, following set rules.

igp.desc: Protected Geographical Indication: an EU mark for products with at least one production stage in the area of origin.

evo.desc: Extra virgin olive oil: pressed from olives by mechanical means only.

taggiasche.desc: Small olives from Liguria: sweet and delicate.

crusco.desc: A sweet pepper from Senise, dried then fried: crisp, not hot.

riso-venere.desc: Italian black wholegrain rice: fragrant, with a firm bite.

tarallo.desc: A small savoury ring-shaped cracker from Puglia.

radicchio.desc: A red chicory from the Veneto, pleasantly bitter.

passata.desc: Sieved fresh tomato purée, uncooked and thick.

carmela.desc: A Campanian brand of peeled tomatoes, not an ingredient in itself.
